name: Stretch mark surgery / tummy tuck

lead: A tummy tuck (abdominoplasty) removes excess skin and fat from the abdomen and tightens the abdominal wall, giving a flatter midsection. Stretch marks lying within the removed skin, mainly below the navel, go with it.

It is usually sought after pregnancy or major weight loss, and is described as mainly cosmetic with some reconstructive benefit for skin folds and muscle separation. Wikipedia and Grokipedia describe it as a contouring operation and do not address stretch marks directly.

paras: Under general anesthesia, skin and fat are excised through a hip-to-hip incision above the pubic area, the muscle fascia is tightened and the navel repositioned. Operating time is 2 to 5 hours, and recovery takes weeks to months.

Wikipedia reports complication rates higher than many other cosmetic surgeries, including seroma, hematoma, infection, wound separation, necrosis, thick or widened scars, numbness, blood clots and anesthesia complications. Smoking, obesity and diabetes raise risk, and it leaves a hip-to-hip scar.

web.title: Stretch mark surgery / tummy tuck — Grokipedia

angle.text: Abdominoplasty removes loose abdominal skin and fat and tightens the muscle, so the midsection looks flatter and stretch marks on the removed skin go with it. People seek it after pregnancy or major weight loss, and the change is visible after healing.

lead: Abdominoplasty, commonly called a tummy tuck, is a surgical procedure that removes excess skin and fat from the abdomen and tightens the underlying muscle and fascia.[1][2] It is typically sought after pregnancy or major weight loss, including after bariatric surgery, when loose skin and stretched abdominal muscles persist despite diet and exercise.[1]

In looksmaxxing and body-image discussions it is mentioned as a surgical option for stretch marks on lower abdominal skin, since the marks are removed if they lie within the excised tissue. Wikipedia and Grokipedia describe the operation chiefly as a contouring procedure and do not discuss striae removal specifically.[1][2]

The surgery is described as generally safe and effective when performed by qualified plastic surgeons, but with complication rates higher than many other cosmetic surgeries because of the extent of dissection.[2]
infobox: Hip to hip, above pubic area

paras: The operation removes skin and fat from the middle and lower abdomen, plicates the rectus abdominis fascia, and repositions the navel. Variations include full, mini, extended and fleur-de-lis abdominoplasty, chosen according to anatomy, amount of excess skin and fat distribution.[1][2]

Grokipedia describes ideal candidates as healthy adults with stable weight for at least six months, BMI typically under 30, non-smokers, no plans for future pregnancy and realistic expectations. It lists uncontrolled diabetes, severe cardiopulmonary disease and coagulopathy as contraindications and notes psychological screening for body dysmorphic disorder.[1]
Beyond cosmetic goals, reconstructive indications include chronic skin irritation or infection beneath an overhanging abdominal fold and diastasis recti.[1]

Stretch marks are dermal scars caused by skin stretching and are not removed by topical treatment in any clearly established way.[3] In abdominoplasty, skin below the navel is excised and the remaining skin pulled down, so striae in that region may be removed while marks above the navel or elsewhere may remain or be displaced. The sources reviewed do not quantify this.

Reported complications include seroma, hematoma, infection, delayed healing or wound separation, skin or fat necrosis, thickened or widened scars, numbness, asymmetry, deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, and anesthesia-related events.[2] Smoking, obesity, diabetes, prior abdominal surgery and combined procedures such as liposuction are listed as higher-risk factors.[2]

Published case series and reviews analysing abdominoplasty complications include a 206-case university hospital review, an 86-patient series, and a review of risk factors and safety of combined procedures.[4][5][6] Progressive tension sutures and seroma-prevention techniques have been studied to reduce local complications.[7][8]

Grokipedia states that Demars and Marx performed the first recorded dermolipectomy in 1890 during an umbilical hernia repair, that Howard Kelly described abdominal lipectomy in 1899, and that Max Thorek developed an umbilicus-preserving technique in 1924.[1] Wikipedia says modern versions developed from the 1960s.[2]

Studies of abdominoplasty itself include retrospective complication analyses and randomised or registered trials of technique, for example a completed phase 4 registration of the effects of abdominoplasty and liposuction in 143 patients and trials examining Scarpa fascia preservation and seroma after abdominoplasty.[9][10][4][5][6] These studies address complications and surgical technique rather than stretch mark removal. No studies found that evaluate abdominoplasty specifically as a treatment for stretch marks.

timeline.event: Demars and Marx perform the first recorded dermolipectomy.[1]
Max Thorek develops an umbilicus-preserving technique.[1]
Modern abdominoplasty techniques begin to develop.[2]
